rules.title: Stage what you own, never rewrite history
rules.text: A script stages and pushes only the paths it owns: `git add -A` sweeps a sibling's half-finished files into someone else's commit, and an amend or a force-push rewrites commits another writer has already pulled.

judgement.question: Would this line stage files another writer owns, or rewrite history someone else has already pulled?

criteria.true: it stages everything or rewrites history, putting a sibling's in-flight work or another writer's commits at risk
criteria.false: it names the paths it stages and pushes without rewriting, or it operates on a throwaway fixture outside the repository
